set_aside.subject: Admission verdict production
set_aside.text: “Admission is one recorded verdict over the whole active corpus” does not say how many times each case is executed or how passing and failing executions are selected when an implementation can vary through an undetected source of time or chance.
set_aside.question: For one admission attempt, exactly which executions determine the recorded verdict: one execution per case, repeated executions under a stated rule, or previously recorded trial evidence?
options: Execute every active case once and aggregate those executions
Execute cases repeatedly under a specified acceptance rule
Derive the verdict from existing trial evidence rather than new executions
set_aside.default_guess: Execute every active case once in the sandbox and admit only if every execution passes.

witness.initial: A contract has one trial case, and its implementation obtains chance through a method the sandbox does not detect; it sometimes returns the expected value and sometimes violates the output expectation.
events: The kernel performs admission over the active corpus.
outcomes: The kernel executes the case once, observes a passing result, records `admitted`, and activates the implementation.
The kernel repeats the case or selects another available execution, observes a failure, and refuses admission.
witness.observer: The agent sees whether the implementation becomes active, and later flow runners see different executable behavior.

set_aside.subject: Identity and cardinality of recorded admission verdicts
set_aside.text: “Admission is one recorded verdict” does not identify what the verdict is recorded against or whether “one” means one per implementation, one per implementation and corpus state, or one per submission attempt.
set_aside.question: What uniquely identifies an admission verdict, and may the same implementation receive another verdict when submitted again against an unchanged corpus?
options: One immutable verdict per implementation identity
One verdict per implementation identity and exact corpus revision
A new verdict for every submission attempt
set_aside.default_guess: Record one immutable verdict per implementation identity and exact corpus revision; return it on an identical resubmission while that corpus revision remains current.

witness.initial: An implementation has already received a failing verdict against the current corpus, but its behavior is nondeterministic through an undetected source.
events: The agent submits byte-identical code again, so authoring resolves to the existing implementation identity.
outcomes: The kernel returns the existing failing verdict and refuses activation because that implementation already has its one verdict.
The kernel performs another admission attempt, records a passing verdict, and activates the same implementation identity.
witness.observer: The submitting agent sees whether resubmission can change admission and activation.

set_aside.subject: Admission after the trial corpus changes
set_aside.text: “Each contract version has a trial corpus” and “Admission is one recorded verdict over the whole active corpus” do not say what happens to recorded verdicts and the current activation when a new case is added.
set_aside.question: When the corpus gains a case, does an earlier admitted verdict cease to qualify immediately, is the active implementation automatically evaluated again, or does it remain active until a later submission or explicit admission action?
options: Invalidate prior verdicts and automatically re-admit the active implementation
Invalidate prior verdicts and leave the contract version without a current activation until an implementation is submitted
Keep the existing activation but require a verdict over the enlarged corpus only for later activation or rollback
Treat the old verdict as still admitted if the implementation later passes the added case during another action
set_aside.default_guess: Keep historical verdicts but make them ineligible for activation or rollback against the enlarged corpus; do not run code automatically, and require a later implementation submission to obtain a new verdict.

witness.initial: Implementation I is admitted and active for contract version C over corpus {A}.
events: An authoring agent adds failing regression case B to C's corpus.
Before any new implementation is submitted, an owner or agent starts a flow using C.
outcomes: I remains active, so the run starts and may execute behavior that fails B.
I's verdict no longer covers the current corpus, so its activation is removed or unusable and the run is refused for having no current activation.
witness.observer: The flow starter sees whether a run is created; downstream users may also see the old implementation execute.
